prompt: Match each kind of KMS key to who decides its policy.

pairs.right: AWS, and it is not in the account
AWS; the account can read it
The team, in the key policy

prompt: Why pay for a customer managed key when aws/ssm costs no monthly fee?

choices.text: Customer managed keys encrypt more strongly
choices.why: Both are 256-bit AES in the same hardware.

choices.text: AWS managed keys expire after a year
choices.why: They do not expire.

choices.text: Control over who uses the key, in its policy
choices.why: Right. A key policy the team writes, and the power to disable or delete.

choices.text: Only customer managed keys are recorded in CloudTrail
choices.why: Every KMS request is recorded.

prompt: A key policy is edited to remove the statement that gives the account's root principal kms:*. What happens to IAM policies that allow kms:Decrypt on that key?
hint: Which policy is the root of access?

choices.text: They stop mattering
choices.why: Right. That statement is what hands the decision to IAM.

choices.text: They keep working, since IAM is checked first
choices.why: The key policy is the root; IAM counts only if it delegates.

choices.text: The key is disabled until the statement returns
choices.why: The key stays enabled; access changes.

choices.text: The root user loses access but administrators keep it
choices.why: Administrators' IAM permissions stop mattering too.

prompt: Why did decrypt not need the key's id?

choices.text: moto guesses the only key there is
choices.why: AWS behaves the same with many keys.

choices.text: The alias is stored in the profile
choices.why: Nothing was configured.

choices.text: Decrypt uses the default key of the account
choices.why: There is no such default for decrypt.

choices.text: The ciphertext names its key
choices.why: Right. KMS reads it from the ciphertext.

prompt: A ciphertext was made with --encryption-context order=1001. What does decrypting it without a context do?

choices.text: It succeeds, since the context is not secret
choices.why: Not secret, and still required.

choices.text: It fails with InvalidCiphertextException
choices.why: Right. The context is required, though not secret.

choices.text: It succeeds and returns the context too
choices.why: The context is not stored in the ciphertext.

choices.text: It asks for the key's id instead
choices.why: The key is in the ciphertext; the context is not.

prompt: The most that KMS Encrypt accepts in one request is ____ bytes.
In envelope encryption, what does the KMS key encrypt?

choices.text: Only the data key
choices.why: Right. The data is encrypted locally with the data key.

choices.text: The file, in 4 KB pieces
choices.why: That would be one request per piece; envelope encryption avoids it.

choices.text: The file's name and size
choices.why: Neither is encrypted by KMS.

choices.text: Both the file and the data key
choices.why: The file never goes to KMS.

prompt: How many requests to KMS does envelope.py make to seal a 5 MB file?
Where does envelope.py keep the plaintext data key after sealing?

choices.text: In orders.csv.sealed, base64-encoded
choices.why: The file holds the encrypted data key, not the plain one.

choices.text: In ~/.aws, beside the credentials
choices.why: Nothing is written there.

choices.text: Nowhere
choices.why: Right. It is gone when the function returns.

choices.text: In KMS, under the alias
choices.why: KMS does not keep data keys.

prompt: Put the steps of sealing a file in order.
items: Ask KMS for a data key
Encrypt the file locally with the plain data key
Write the data and the encrypted data key together

prompt: After a KMS key is rotated, what happens to data encrypted before the rotation?

choices.text: It must be re-encrypted within 30 days
choices.why: Nothing is re-encrypted.

choices.text: It becomes unreadable
choices.why: That is deletion, not rotation.

choices.text: It decrypts only with the old key id
choices.why: The id does not change on rotation.

choices.text: It still decrypts, with the old material
choices.why: Right. KMS keeps old material for the life of the key.

prompt: moto decrypted with a key in PendingDeletion. What does AWS do, and why does it matter?
hint: The waiting period has a purpose.

choices.text: Refuses, so what still needs the key breaks inside the window
choices.why: Right. KMSInvalidStateException, inside the window.

choices.text: Decrypts too; the key works until the deletion date
choices.why: A pending key cannot be used at all on AWS.

choices.text: Decrypts and sends an e-mail to the account owner
choices.why: There is no such e-mail; that alarm is the team's to build.

choices.text: Re-encrypts the data under a new key
choices.why: KMS never touches the data.

prompt: A deletion is cancelled. What state is the key in?

choices.text: Enabled
choices.why: Cancelling does not put a key back into use.

choices.text: Disabled
choices.why: Right. It must be enabled on purpose.

choices.text: PendingImport
choices.why: That is for imported key material.

choices.text: PendingDeletion, with a new date
choices.why: The deletion is cancelled.

prompt: What is the shortest waiting period, in days, that schedule-key-deletion accepts?
An S3 bucket receives 4 million objects a month with SSE-KMS and no Bucket Key. At 0.03 USD per 10,000 requests, what do the writes cost in KMS requests, in USD?
A customer managed key is rotated once a year. Per AWS's documentation, what is its monthly fee in USD after the third rotation?
hint: The first two rotations add a fee; later ones do not.

prompt: Which of these does KMS behave the same on in moto and on AWS? Choose all that apply.
hint: One of them is moto's mistake.

choices.text: Refusing a decrypt without the encryption context
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Refusing to encrypt more than 4,096 bytes
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Leaving a key Disabled after a cancelled deletion
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Decrypting with a key pending deletion
choices.why: moto does; AWS refuses.

choices.text: Reporting the rotation period
choices.why: moto reports only whether rotation is on.
